newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish PM expected to announce cabinet reshuffle.
newsitem.headline: Swedish PM expected to announce cabinet reshuffle.

text.p: Swedish Prime Minister Goran Persson was expected to announce a reshuffle of his cabinet later on Tuesday, Swedish radio reported, but the Swedish leader's press secretary declined comment on the subject.
The radio was quoting the on-line pages of political daily newspaper Dagens Politik.

Persson did, however, call a special cabinet session. "There will be an extra cabinet meeting today but I have no information on exactly when it will be," the prime minister's spokesman, Leif-Ake Falk, told Reuters.

Persson has made no major changes to cabinet since he took over the leadership of the ruling Social Democrats Party and became prime minister last March. He replaced Ingvar Carlsson who retired from politics.
Dagens Politik said the most likely changes would probably be minor but aimed at putting more weight into Persson's inner cabinet and centralise his power base.
Sweden's political parties are beginning to jockey for the next general election due in September 1998.
Persson is likely to appoint Industry and Commerce Minister Bjorn Von Sydow as Sweden's new defence minister, replacing Thage Peterson, Dagens Politik's home page said.
Peterson, a leading member of the Social Democrats and heavyweight in parliament, was likely to be given a position in the inner cabinet, replacing Leif Pagrotsky.

Petersson was a member of the inner cabinet of former prime minister Olof Palme, who was shot dead in a Stockholm street in 1986, and who is viewed as being among the country's most experienced politicians.

Pagrotsky would probably be offered the position of industry and commerce minister in what would be the first government portfolio job for a politician widely viewed as being a favourite of Persson's, the paper said.
